Made for curious ears.Record. Learn. Wander.

Make a landscape you can hear.

Draw & record. Enable the microphone first. Then hold down and draw while making your mouth sound. Recording starts with the stroke and stops when you release. Each location remembers that moment of your voice. Draw slowly, over a few seconds.

Small sounds. You don’t need a separate point tool: hold nearly still while recording, then release. A tiny stroke is treated as one sustained sound.

For a sine-shaped line, sing high at its peaks and low at its troughs while drawing. The shape does not automatically set pitch: your recorded voice does. Draw without crossing back over the same place for an unambiguous sound path.

Learn. Press Learn sounds. Tiny strokes use a representative active section, as before. Lines use a sequence of short active sections, retaining their recording times. Silent sections are skipped and bridged with neighboring active sounds.

Explore. Move around the canvas. Along a line, the sound follows the corresponding moment in its recording. Between anchors, their local sound qualities are morphed. Focus the canvas and use arrow keys if you prefer.

Uploads or replacement recordings for an existing line map beginning to end by distance along its path. Drawing and recording together gives precise timing. At crossings, one place can represent multiple times: the nearest segment determines the line position; separate crossing anchors share influence.

These are synthesized approximations, not exact audio replays or a physical mouth simulation. Your sounds are stored locally. Start over clears this landscape; older two-sound recordings are kept separately.
